manual.title: Trauma Response Simulator Manual
manual.subtitle: What the simulator does, how it works, and why it is built this way
manual.description: A searchable guide to the browser game, its local-only companion tools, and the boundaries maintainers must preserve. Player instructions remain in [README.md](../README.md); content-pack details remain in [AUTHORING.md](../AUTHORING.md).
manual.footer: T.R.S. {{project.version}} · Facts are linked to their evidence; inferred rationale is labeled.

sections.title: The Simulation
sections.description: The player-facing loop, its hidden response model, and the modes that change a run.

entries.title: Turn loop and endings
entries.summary: Choose a response, absorb hidden stat changes, and continue until an ending condition wins.
entries.what: Presents a sequence of everyday stressors. Each choice changes Repression, Social Mask, and Inner Child until a failure threshold or the mode's turn limit produces an ending.
how: `handleChoice()` applies the choice effects and any unlocked mechanism modifier, clamps stats to 0–100, and updates the turn log.
`checkGameEnd()` evaluates failure thresholds and the turn limit; otherwise the engine loads another event.
entries.why: The loop makes coping patterns legible through accumulated consequences rather than a single right-answer quiz. This intent is recorded in the player explanation and reinforced by D-003's hidden-effects rule.

entries.title: Hidden trauma responses and mechanisms
entries.summary: Every choice is tagged fawn, flight, fight, freeze, or secure, but the label and effects stay hidden until after the choice.
entries.what: Tracks how often the player chooses each of five response identities. Repeating one three times unlocks its coping mechanism, whose modifier affects later choices with the same tag.
entries.how: Choice objects carry a `tag` and stat effects. `handleChoice()` increments the matching counter, unlocks the pack-defined mechanism at `config.unlockThreshold`, and adds its `mod` to later matching effects. The interface exposes neither the tag nor numerical outcome before selection.
entries.why: D-003 records the deliberate rule: choices should feel like real reactions under uncertainty, not visible arithmetic that can be optimized before clicking.

entries.title: Modes, seeds, and timed events
entries.summary: Standard, Extended Therapy, and Arcade reuse one engine while changing limits, scaling, and starting state.
entries.what: Supports a finite standard run, an unlockable longer and more volatile Extended Therapy run, and an endless escalating Arcade run. Optional timed events can choose a response when the clock expires. Standard and Extended Therapy runs can replay a supplied seed.
how: `hashSeed()` and `mulberry32()` create the run's deterministic random-number generator; in-run draws use `state.rng`.
Mode flags select the turn limit, effect multiplier, fixed or rolled starting stats, and Arcade escalation tier.
Timed events use pack-wide chance and duration values, with per-event opt-out or duration overrides.
entries.why: Seeds make comparisons and bug reports repeatable. The alternate modes extend replay value without creating separate engines. The shared-engine rationale is inferred from the common state and functions in `js/engine.js`; deterministic replay is an explicit architecture invariant.

entries.title: Result sharing
entries.summary: Sharing is an explicit, on-device handoff after a run ends.
entries.what: Builds a text summary or portrait image containing the ending, stats, seed, optional player name, and acquired mechanisms. The player can copy, download, or invoke the device share sheet.
entries.how: Canvas helpers in `js/engine.js` render the image locally. `navigator.share` receives the generated file when supported; desktop fallback downloads it, while the text path writes only after the player requests a copy.
entries.why: The explicit handoff preserves the project's local-only promise while still making results portable. No result is transmitted automatically.

sections.title: Persistent Features
sections.description: State that survives a run stays in the browser and has explicit reset behavior.

entries.title: Case Files
entries.summary: A cross-run archive reveals only endings and mechanisms the player has actually encountered.
entries.what: Records discovered survival-ending variants, failure-ending variants, and coping mechanisms. Undiscovered entries remain redacted.
entries.how: `js/codex.js` stores slot indexes and mechanism keys under `uct_codex_v1`. A signature derived from ending-pool sizes and mechanism keys detects incompatible content-pack shapes and resets the archive instead of mislabeling old discoveries.
entries.why: The archive gives repeat runs a persistent collection goal without revealing choice effects or ending conditions. Numbered cases preserve D-003's hidden-information boundary.

entries.title: Field Log
entries.summary: A sincere journal sits beside the game but is not part of the simulation.
entries.what: Lets a player record a real event, their response, body sensations, what helped, and optional response tags. It includes a notice that it is a self-tracking tool rather than therapy or crisis support.
entries.how: `js/field-log.js` renders and stores entries under `uct_field_log_v1`. Its mode shares the page shell with the simulation but has separate state and a separate deletion confirmation.
entries.why: D-004 records that the journal is real user material: its language stays sincere, its crisis notice stays intact, and bulk game-data reset may not silently erase it.

entries.title: Local state and reset boundaries
entries.summary: All durable state lives in named `localStorage` keys, and the old `uct_*` prefix is permanent.
entries.what: Persists the custom pack, Case Files, Extended Therapy unlock, Arcade score, player name, Timed Events preference, and Field Log without an account or server.
entries.how: Feature modules read and write their established keys. `resetAllGameData()` removes simulation data after one confirmation, then asks separately whether to remove the Field Log.
entries.why: D-001 keeps the game serverless, D-002 preserves existing saves across the product rename, and D-004 protects journal entries from the ordinary reset path.

sections.title: Content System
sections.description: Events, wording, tuning, endings, and display names travel together as one validated content pack.

entries.title: Content-pack contract
entries.summary: One JSON-compatible structure supplies the simulator's authored content and tunable behavior.
entries.what: Defines config values, zones, the five mechanisms, glitch logs, failure endings, survival endings, and events. A saved custom pack replaces the built-in default when it passes validation.
entries.how: Classic scripts assemble `DEFAULT_CONTENT`; `getContent()` reads `uct_custom_content_v1`, parses it, and falls back to the default when `contentPackProblems()` finds a run-breaking structural problem.
entries.why: Keeping text and tuning together lets a content pack reskin the whole simulation without changing the engine. The separation follows D-001's dependency-free static architecture and the authoring contract.

entries.title: Content editor
entries.summary: A separate static page edits, validates, imports, exports, saves, and resets content packs.
entries.what: Provides form controls for the content-pack structure and a draft workflow that can be previewed in the game after saving.
entries.how: `editor.html` loads the content globals and `js/editor.js`. The editor keeps a draft in memory, writes the full pack to the shared storage key only on Save, exports JSON, and validates imported JSON before making it the current draft.
entries.why: Explicit Save prevents partial edits from overwriting a working pack. Keeping the editor separate from the game preserves the simple two-page static deployment. This rationale is recorded in `AUTHORING.md`.

entries.title: Content validation and rendering safety
entries.summary: Imported and saved packs are untrusted input even though the game has no server.
entries.what: Rejects pack shapes that would break a run and displays pack-authored strings as text rather than executable markup.
entries.how: `contentPackProblems()` checks required collections, known mechanism tags, numeric config and modifier values, and effect shapes. Rendering paths use `textContent` for pack strings; the smoke test includes a Case Files escaping check and malformed-pack fallback check.
entries.why: A local JSON file can still contain hostile markup or invalid values. Treating it as untrusted preserves the static app's trust boundary without forbidding community content.

sections.title: Maintenance and Boundaries
sections.description: The repository remains portable by keeping runtime structure small, verification explicit, and the SCI0 port outside this checkout.

entries.title: Static runtime and script order
entries.summary: The game runs from `file://` or any static host with no build step or runtime dependency.
entries.what: Ships as plain HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Players can open `index.html` directly; contributors may also use a local static server.
entries.how: Classic `<script>` tags load shared globals in dependency order: content fragments, content assembly, Case Files, engine, Field Log, and main-page controls. The editor loads the same content base followed by its own controller.
entries.why: D-001 records the trade-off: universal static delivery and no dependency tree are worth relying on globals and a deliberate script order.

entries.title: Verification workflow
entries.summary: Small dependency-free checks cover pack structure, the main browser paths, documentation consistency, and this manual.
entries.what: Provides repeatable checks for content validity, a seeded Chromium playthrough, JavaScript syntax, documentation references, and 3x manual structure and generation.
how: Run `node tools/check-content.js` for the default and shared packs.
Run `node tools/smoke-test.js` for the browser paths and deterministic replay.
Run `python3 tools/check_docs.py` for the Markdown documentation set.
Run `python3 tools/manual.py check docs/trs.manual.json` and rebuild `docs/manual.html` for manual changes.
entries.why: D-001 rules out an installed test stack, so the committed checks use platform tools and standard libraries. The 3x source is validated separately because `check_docs.py` checks document relationships rather than the manual schema.

entries.title: SCI0 port boundary
entries.summary: This repository owns generators for the DOS port, but not the port's generated sources or current state.
entries.what: Transforms browser-game content into source material consumed by the SCI0 port in `github.com/aedmark/TRS_SCI`.
entries.how: Node scripts under `tools/` read the canonical JavaScript content and write through `tools/lib/sci-paths.js` into `TRS_SCI_DIR`, defaulting to a separate local checkout. Port outputs are committed there rather than here.
entries.why: The browser game is the canonical content source while SCI-specific compiled artifacts belong with the port. The exact long-term home of the generators remains open as Q-001, so this manual records the current boundary without presenting that placement as settled intent.
